message.content: The sea typically looks blue—especially when it's clear and deep—because water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum and scatters blue light. In shallower or more vegetated waters it can appear greenish, while in very shallow or sandy areas it may look turquoise or even a pale yellowish hue. The exact shade depends on depth, clarity, angle of sunlight, and the presence of algae or sediment.
